overlooked_assumption: _xirr assumes the first cashflow is an investment (negative amount) and the last is a return (positive amount), but the caller passes a negative start amount and a positive ending amount without recognizing that the function requires at least one intermediate positive cashflow to compute a meaningful IRR, or that the sign convention must include both an outflow and inflow beyond the endpoints.
why_it_breaks: The _xirr function computes IRR via Newton-Raphson on NPV and dNPV. With only two cashflows (-100000 on 2024-01-02 and +106000 on 2024-01-12), the NPV function becomes linear in rate: NPV(rate) = -100000/(1+rate)^0 + 106000/(1+rate)^(10/365). The derivative dNPV also has a fixed sign for all positive rates, so Newton never converges to a root and the loop exits without setting a rate, leaving the IRR as None (rendered as n/a). The agent overlooked that _xirr requires at least three cashflow points (an initial outflow, an intermediate inflow/outflow, and a final amount) for the nonlinearity needed for convergence, or that the sign convention must ensure the derivative changes sign.
